title: Japan — Northern Alps in autumn
notes: Fifteen nights, sequenced north to south and high to low so it follows the autumn colour down the mountain rather than fighting it, opening with a night at Nagano for Zenkoji and closing with one in Tokyo. The dates are a deliberate trade: Hakuba's alpine colour peaks late September, the Nakasendo's peaks late October, and five weeks apart they cannot both be caught in one trip — so this window takes Hakuba at its best and accepts the Kiso valley before its peak and Kamikochi in maples rather than golden larch. Happo Pond decided it: reported at peak on 11 Oct in both 2024 and 2025, and it gets four nights and two headline walks here. The cost is Sports Day on 11 Oct, which the trip is arranged around rather than against: the holiday weekend is spent in Nagano, a city, and the drive over to Hakuba happens on the Monday itself, against the traffic heading home. Nothing is booked yet. Every remark on this page comes from the file and is replaced whenever the plan changes; the private notes behind sign-in are yours and are never written to from here.

summary.note: Budget figures are the whole trip for two travellers, in MYR, and are planning estimates rather than quotes — nothing is booked. They exclude flights. The exchange rate is the mid-market rate on 14 Aug 2026 (1 MYR = 38.9 JPY), a placeholder until money is actually changed; every converted figure on the site moves with it. Day costs carry only fares that have been looked up and checked, as a group total for two, so the daily totals are well below what a day will really cost — the planning envelope is this table, not those. Shopping is deliberately not here and is tracked separately; Miscellaneous is contingency, not a shopping allowance.

days.summary: Arrival only — nothing planned, so the first full day starts rested.

items.activity: Check in at KLIA for NH886
items.remarks: Three hours before a 14:15 departure.

items.activity: Fly Kuala Lumpur (KUL) to Tokyo Haneda (HND)
Land at Haneda, clear immigration and collect bags

Travel to the hotel
Haneda (HND) -(Walk)> Hotel
items.remarks: Airport hotel — the late landing is deliberate and there is nothing worth a train ride at this hour.

days.summary: Tokyo to Nagano, and an afternoon at Zenkoji.

items.activity:
Travel to Tokyo Station
Hotel -(Tokyo Monorail)> Hamamatsucho Station -(JR Yamanote Line)> Tokyo Station
items.remarks: About 17 minutes on the monorail from Haneda Terminal 3, then 5 on the Yamanote — allow 30 with the change and the bags. The Keikyu line to Shinagawa and JR across is the same journey by another route if the monorail is queued.

items.activity:
Travel to Nagano
Tokyo Station -(Hokuriku Shinkansen)> Nagano Station
items.remarks: Three services run this line and they are not interchangeable. Kagayaki is fastest at about 80 minutes but is entirely reserved — there are no unreserved cars at all, so turning up hoping to board one does not work. Hakutaka takes about 95 minutes and Asama, which terminates at Nagano, a little longer; both carry unreserved seats. JPY 8,340 per person reserved, JPY 7,680 unreserved — figure shown is reserved for two. No oversized-baggage reservation is needed here: that rule covers the Tokaido, Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen only, and the Hokuriku is first come, first served.

items.activity: Check in, then lunch at Nagano
items.remarks: Nagano is soba country. One night here rather than a bus-gap stop, which is what turns Zenkoji from a rushed hour into an afternoon.

1,400 years old, and it holds the first Buddhist statue ever brought to Japan — kept hidden, never shown. The part people remember is the kaidan meguri: a pitch-dark passage under the main hall where you feel along the wall for the key to paradise. JPY 1,200 per person for the combined ticket, JPY 600 for just the inner sanctuary and passage; figure shown is the combined for two. Allow two hours inside, plus another for the approach street. About 15 minutes by bus from the station, or 30 on foot straight up the main road.

If tomorrow's bus is a late one, Zenkoji holds a morning service at dawn — 05:30 to 07:00 depending on sunrise, led by the head priests, and one of the few daily temple rituals in Japan still open to the public. A better hour there than any afternoon.

days.summary: Five shrines up a mountainside, through 400-year-old cedars.

items.activity:
Travel to Togakushi
Nagano Station -(Alpico Bus)> Togakushi Okusha
items.remarks: Just over an hour, JPY 1,550 per person each way; figure shown is the return for two. Green season runs eleven departures a day from Nagano Station, 06:50 to 14:10, so this is a far easier bus than the Hakuba one. Three things the operator is specific about: every seat is reserved (book online, which opens a month ahead — you can board without one if there is space, but not reliably), Suica and the other IC cards do NOT work so bring cash or a contactless Visa, and the old Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass was discontinued in 2025, so do not plan around it.

items.activity:
Walk the cedar avenue to Okusha
Togakushi Okusha -(Hike - 40 mins)> Togakushi Okusha Shrine
items.remarks: A 2 km approach through the thatched Zuijinmon gate and then 300-odd Japanese cedars, many of them 400 years old. The cedars are evergreen, so the avenue looks the same whatever the date — which is the point today, because Togakushi sits at about 1,200 m and peaks late October, so the colour around it will only be turning.
Togakushi is one of Japan's three great soba regions. Eaten here with sansai tempura — battered mountain vegetables.

The middle shrine, about 40 minutes down through the forest from Okusha. Carry on another 2 km to Hokosha for the full five-shrine walk, or stop here — the whole traverse is 10-12 km. Use the Togakushi Shuttle Bus to move about within the area.

items.activity:
Travel to Nagano
Togakushi Chusha -(Alpico Bus)> Nagano Station
items.remarks: Last bus of the day leaves the campsite at 16:20 and reaches Nagano at 17:25. Earlier ones run roughly hourly through the afternoon.

days.summary: Over to Hakuba on the holiday, and a terrace above the valley.

items.activity: Collect the hire car at Nagano Station
items.remarks: The car covers the next four days - Hakuba, Matsumoto and Azumino - and goes back at Matsumoto. Both are in Nagano prefecture, which is the whole point: a one-way drop inside one prefecture is free or close to it, where Nagano to Nagoya would have run to tens of thousands.

items.activity:
Check out and drive to Hakuba
Nagano Station -(Drive)> Hakuba Station
items.remarks: About 1h 15m, and deliberately on Sports Day itself. The holiday traffic on a Monday runs the other way - people leaving the resorts for the cities - so going north into Hakuba is against the flow, and tonight is the first quiet night in the valley after the long weekend rather than the last busy one. The rental desk will be busy with returns, so allow a little longer at the counter.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags

Explore Hakuba Iwatake Mountain Harbor
Hotel -(Drive)> Hakuba Iwatake Mountain Resort
items.remarks: The gentle option for an arrival afternoon: the Noah gondola climbs eight minutes to a terrace at 1,289 m looking straight across at the Northern Alps, with THE CITY BAKERY and a couple of other places to eat on the deck. Green season runs 08:30-17:00 with the last ride up at 16:20 and the last down at 16:50, and the bakery shuts at 16:00 - so this is an afternoon, not an evening.

Hakuba Happo Onsen is highly alkaline at pH 11 and over, and is Japan's only natural hydrogen hot spring, which is what the silky-water reputation is about. Four public baths if the hotel has none of its own: Happo-no-Yu (JPY 1,000, 10:00-21:00, daily), Obinata-no-Yu (JPY 700, 11:00-21:00), Mimizuku-no-Yu (JPY 1,000 but only 13:00-17:00 for non-guests) and Sato-no-Yu.

days.summary: The classic Hakuba walk, on the best date the trip can give it.

items.remarks: Start early. The trail is high and completely exposed, and the light on the Alps is best before the afternoon cloud builds.

items.activity:
Travel to Happo-one
Hotel -(Drive)> Happo Gondola Adam
items.remarks: Ten minutes or so from most of the village, with parking at the gondola base.

items.activity: Ride the Alpen Line to Happo Ike Sanso
items.remarks: Three stages - the Adam gondola, then the Alpen Quad and Grat Quad chairlifts - about 20-25 minutes in total, ending at the Happo Ike Sanso lodge at roughly 1,830 m. JPY 3,500 per person return for the full line; figure shown is for two. Check the last descent before you start walking: uphill service stops 30 minutes before the final Grat Quad, and the green season ends on 3 Nov.

items.activity:
Hike to Happo Pond
Happo Ike Sanso -(Hike - 90 mins)> Happo Pond
items.remarks: 3.3 km round trip and about 230 m of climb, to the pond at 2,060 m. Just above the lodge the path forks and it is worth knowing which is which: the LEFT branch is mostly wooden boardwalk and much easier underfoot, the RIGHT is rocky and uneven. They rejoin higher up, so take the boardwalk going up and decide about the rocks on the way down. Estimates vary widely - the operator's own guide says 1.5 to 2 hours up and an hour down, other sources say 45 minutes; budget two hours and be pleased if it is less. Cairns mark the way and there is a small stone shrine at the pond.

The reflection is the whole point, so it wants a still morning. This is also why the trip sits where it does: the pond was reported at peak on 11 Oct in both 2024 and 2025, so today is a single day past two years of observed peak, and on an ordinary Tuesday rather than yesterday's holiday. Two warnings from the operator worth repeating - the trail has no shelter at all from wind or rain, so windproof layers are not optional, and it wants proper hiking shoes rather than trainers.

items.activity:
Return to Hakuba
Happo Pond -(Hike - 60 mins)> Happo Ike Sanso
items.remarks: About an hour down, then the lifts. If this morning was clouded in, today and tomorrow's Tsugaike can swap - that is the only spare card the three nights hold.

days.summary: Six kilometres of boardwalk over four marshes, at your own speed.

items.activity:
Travel to Tsugaike
Hotel -(Drive)> Tsugaike Kogen
items.remarks: About 25 minutes north, and the clearest case for having the car up here - the bus to Tsugaike is sparse.

items.activity: Ride the gondola and ropeway to Tsugaike Nature Park
items.remarks: The Eve gondola takes about 20 minutes, then the ropeway another six, landing near the Visitor Center at roughly 1,900 m. JPY 3,700 per person return including park entry, or JPY 3,300 if bought at a Seven-Eleven beforehand - figure shown is the gate price for two. The Visitor Center runs 08:30-16:40 and the park closes for the season at the end of October. Confirm the gondola is not in its late-October maintenance window.

Around 6 km of raised boardwalk across four marshes - Mizubasho, Watasuge, Ukishima and Tenbo. Pick the length to suit the day: there are 1 km, 2 km and 3 km circuits as well as the full 5.5 km loop, which takes about three and a half hours. Watasuge Marsh is the one to reach - the wetland opens out and the Hakuba range stands straight behind it. Boardwalk throughout, so this is walking rather than climbing, and it reads far better in flat light than Happo Pond does, which is why it is the one to move if the weather forces a swap.

items.activity:
Return to Hakuba
Tsugaike Kogen -(Drive)> Hotel

items.remarks: Last night in the valley - worth trying whichever of the four public baths you did not use on the first evening.

days.summary: Down the valley with a wasabi farm on the way, and the car goes back.

items.activity:
Check out and drive to Azumino
Hakuba Station -(Drive)> Daio Wasabi Farm
items.remarks: About 1h 15m south down the valley. Azumino sits directly on the road from Hakuba to Matsumoto, so this is a stop on the way rather than a detour - which is the whole reason the wasabi farm sits on today rather than tomorrow. It saves a there-and-back drive, a day on the hire, and the Matsumoto parking night entirely.

Japan's largest wasabi farm - 15 hectares, free to enter, laid out along clear spring-fed channels with the Alps behind. Its own best season is late Sep to late Oct, so this lands well. The wasabi soft-serve is the thing people come for. Opens at 09:00; the closing time shifts with the season, so check before relying on a late finish.
Wasabi soba at the farm itself, or into Hotaka for something more substantial.

Optional, and the first thing to drop if the day runs long: the Rokuzan Art Museum is beside Hotaka station and the Chihiro Art Museum a little further out. Azumino is also 30 minutes from Matsumoto by train, so anything missed today can be picked up on a spare morning without a car.

items.activity:
Drive to Matsumoto
Daio Wasabi Farm -(Drive)> Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: About 35 minutes. Refuel on the way in - full-to-full is the usual policy.

items.activity: Return the hire car at Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: Four days, and a day earlier than this plan used to have it. Because the car goes back before check-in, there is no Matsumoto parking to arrange at all, and a 16:00 drop leaves real margin against the branch's closing time - the old 17:30 did not. Everything from here is walking, rail or bus: Kamikochi bans private vehicles and the Magome-Tsumago walk is point-to-point.

Local to the city rather than generic: sanzoku-yaki (a whole garlic-soy chicken thigh, fried), basashi, and Shinshu soba - this is one of Japan's best buckwheat regions and the new crop lands in autumn.

days.summary: A whole day in the castle town, all of it on foot.

items.remarks: One of only twelve original keeps left standing in Japan, and a National Treasure. JPY 1,200 per person; figure shown is for two. Open 08:30-17:00 with last admission at 16:30. The keep is climbed by stairs only and they are narrow and steep - go up early, before the queue on them builds.

A few minutes' walk from the castle and worth pairing with it: an 1876 schoolhouse in the Japanese-Western hybrid style of the period, a National Treasure in its own right, reopened in Nov 2024 after three and a half years of earthquake-proofing. JPY 400 per person, 09:00-17:00, last entry 16:30. Combined tickets with the castle exist and save JPY 200-400 - ask at whichever you reach first.

White-walled kura storehouses with black lattice, now craft shops, cafes and sake merchants. Nawate-dori - the frog street along the Metoba river, with nostalgic toy and snack stalls - runs parallel a block north, so the two are one walk.

items.activity: Explore Matsumoto City Museum of Art
items.remarks: Yayoi Kusama is from Matsumoto and the museum holds her work, with the dotted pieces outside. This is also the wet-weather anchor for today, though the whole day is town and holds up in rain.

days.summary: Over the Abo pass into Gifu, and three nights in one ryokan.

items.activity:
Travel to Hirayu Onsen
Matsumoto Bus Terminal -(Alpico Bus)> Hirayu Onsen
items.remarks: About 1h 25m, climbing over the Abo pass and out of Nagano into Gifu. Hirayu is the hub for this whole valley - every road in and out passes through it.
Time it around the connection rather than rushing. Alps Kaido Hirayu at the bus terminal has a free footbath, which is a civilised way to wait.

items.activity:
Travel to Shin-Hotaka Onsen
Hirayu Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Shin-Hotaka Onsen
items.remarks: 32 minutes, JPY 870 per person; figure shown is for two. Roughly hourly, about fifteen departures a day. This one bus threads all five Okuhida villages in order - Hirayu, Fukuji, Shin-Hirayu, Tochio, then Shin-Hotaka - so bath-hopping later is just a matter of getting on it.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags
items.remarks: Three nights in one place, and the point of them is the ryokan's own water rather than touring the valley. Okuhida is said to have more open-air baths than anywhere else in Japan, so choose the property for its rotenburo.
A gentle first afternoon along the Kamata river. There is a free footbath at the ropeway base station, which is also worth a look now so tomorrow starts without hunting for it.

days.summary: Up Japan's only double-decker ropeway, then back down through the trees.

items.activity:
Travel to Shinhotaka Ropeway
Shin-Hotaka Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Shinhotaka Ropeway
items.remarks: The last stop on the line, a few minutes further up from the village.

Two ropeways and a short walk between them. No.1 lifts you from Shinhotaka Onsen station at 1,117 m to Nabedaira Kogen at 1,305 m; you cross to Shirakabadaira at 1,308 m and take No.2 - the double-decker, the only one in Japan - up to Nishi-Hotakaguchi at 2,156 m. About 25 minutes all in. No.1 leaves at :00 and :30 past the hour and No.2 at :15 and :45, so the connection is built in. JPY 3,800 per person return for both; figure shown is for two. Seasonal hours shift - confirm the last descent before you go up.

The rooftop observation deck gives a 360-degree sweep of the Northern Alps - Nishi-Hotaka, Yari and Kasagatake all from the same spot. There is a cafe and a panorama lounge inside for when the wind gets old, which it will: this is 2,156 m in the middle of October, so expect near-freezing and a real chance of early snow. The colour is on the lower stages rather than up here.

Back down to the middle station and into the trees: a 2.3 km loop through the Nabedaira Kogen forest, flat and easy, and the part of the day that is actually autumnal rather than alpine. Guided walks run but need booking ahead.
The Alps Bakery at the middle station does fresh bread, and there is a gelato shop and a view lounge beside it.

There is an open-air bath at the middle station, and a footbath on the platform where you can sit and watch the gondolas come and go. Bathing at 1,300 m with the Hotaka range in front of you is the sort of thing this valley is for.

items.activity:
Travel to the hotel
Shinhotaka Ropeway -(Nohi Bus)> Shin-Hotaka Onsen

days.summary: A slow morning, one waterfall, and the bath.

items.remarks: Deliberately unplanned until the afternoon. This day is also the spare: if yesterday was clouded in at the top, the ropeway moves here and the falls drop off, exactly as Happo Pond and Tsugaike trade places in Hakuba.

items.activity:
Travel to Hirayu Onsen
Shin-Hotaka Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Hirayu Onsen
items.remarks: 32 minutes back down the valley, JPY 870 per person each way; figure shown is the return for two.

items.activity:
Explore Hirayu Great Falls
Hirayu Onsen -(Bus)> Otaki-mae Campsite -(Walk - 20 mins)> Hirayu Great Falls
items.remarks: 64 m of water off the flank of Norikura, one of Japan's hundred famous waterfalls, about 20 minutes on foot from the campsite stop. Late October is when it looks best - the gorge around it colours later than the tops do, so this is one of the few things on the trip that the earlier dates do not shortchange.

Optional, and only if the legs want it: Hirayu no Mori is a large day-use bath complex a short walk from the terminal, with a spread of open-air pools. Otherwise take the bus back and use the ryokan's own.
Last night in the valley. If you have been meaning to try another village's water, the hourly bus makes Tochio or Fukuji an easy hour.

days.summary: One night inside the valley, as the larch starts to turn.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Kamikochi
Shin-Hotaka Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Hirayu Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Kamikochi Bus Terminal
items.remarks: About an hour, changing at Hirayu. Private cars are banned in the valley; bus or taxi only.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags

Explore Taisho Pond
Kamikochi Bus Terminal -(Walk - 45 mins)> Taisho Pond
items.remarks: Flat riverside path along the Azusa.

On these dates the valley is in maples rather than larch: the maple peak is around 17 Oct, so today is two days past it and still good, while the larch does not turn golden until 25 Oct to 5 Nov and will barely have started. That is the trade the earlier window makes — red rather than gold — and it is real rather than a technicality. The densest larch stands, for reference, are around the bus terminal and Konashidaira.
The day-trippers leave on the last buses and the valley empties — this is the whole reason to sleep here.

days.summary: Dawn on the Azusa, then out to the old road.

items.remarks: Mist on Taisho Pond and first light on the Hotaka range — the morning the night here was for.

items.activity:
Hike to Myojin Pond
Kappa Bridge -(Hike - 60 mins)> Myojin Pond
items.remarks: Flat both ways, about 3 hours return with stops.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Tsumago
Kamikochi Bus Terminal -(Alpico Bus)> Shin-Shimashima Station -(Alpico Kamikochi Line)> Matsumoto Station -(JR Shinano Limited Express)> Nagiso Station -(Bus)> Tsumago
items.remarks: About 3 hours all in — a long travel afternoon, down from 1,500 m to about 400 m, where the colour is only now arriving.

items.activity: Check in, then dinner at Tsumago

days.summary: Eight kilometres of the old Nakasendo, at peak colour.

items.remarks: Send the day bags ahead on the Magome-Tsumago forwarding service, which runs in season.
Sloping stone street with the Kiso valley below it.

items.activity:
Hike the Nakasendo to Tsumago
Magome -(Hike - 3 hours)> Tsumago
items.remarks: About 8 km over the Magome pass, 2-3 hours, cedar forest and waterfalls. The classic stretch of the whole route, walked downhill from Magome on purpose — the same eight kilometres uphill is a different day out. This is the day the earlier window costs something: the Kiso valley peaks late Oct into early Nov, so the 21st catches the colour arriving rather than at its best. Good walking either way, and the cedars and the stone paving do not depend on the date.
Preserved with no visible wiring or aerials — best after the day visitors leave.

days.summary: Out of the Kiso valley and into Tokyo, with a day still to spend.

items.remarks: Tsumago before the coaches arrive.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Tokyo
Tsumago -(Bus)> Nagiso Station -(JR Shinano Limited Express)> Nagoya Station -(Tokaido Shinkansen)> Shinagawa Station
items.remarks: About 2 hours to Nagoya — the Kiso valley line ends there, so it is a change rather than a detour — then 1h 40m on. Every Nozomi stops at Shinagawa, which is the Haneda end of Tokyo: getting off there rather than at Tokyo Station saves a leg with the luggage, and is why the hotel is on that side. The second leg is the Tokaido, so unlike the Hokuriku on day 2 the oversized-baggage rule applies — a case whose height, width and depth total 160-250 cm needs a free reserved slot booked with the seat, and boarding without one is a JPY 1,000 charge. Measure before this leg, not at the gate.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags

items.remarks: About 15 minutes from Shinagawa. The Uniqlo and Muji flagships, Ginza Six, and Itoya for stationery.

days.summary: A last day in Tokyo, hands free.

items.activity: Check out and leave the luggage at the hotel
items.remarks: Standard and usually free at a Japanese business hotel — confirm it at check-in rather than on the morning, because the whole day rests on it. Haneda's own coin lockers and baggage counter are the fallback.
About 12 minutes from Shinagawa. Scramble Square and Hikarie for the department stores.
Nakamise-dori for the last of the souvenirs, if the legs are willing. Otherwise stay west and add Shinjuku.
Character Street and the Daimaru food halls are the best single stop for edible souvenirs and ekiben.

items.activity:
Collect luggage, then travel to Haneda
Hotel -(Keikyu Airport Line)> Haneda (HND)
items.remarks: About 15 minutes from Shinagawa on the Keikyu, or 13 on the monorail from Hamamatsucho.

items.activity: Check in at Haneda for NH885
items.remarks: Three hours before a 23:30 departure.

items.activity: Fly Tokyo Haneda (HND) to Kuala Lumpur (KUL)
items.remarks: Lands 06:00 the next morning.

transport.mode: Mixed on purpose. A hire car for the middle four days — Nagano to Hakuba, the Hakuba trailheads, then Matsumoto and Azumino — collected at Nagano Station and returned at Matsumoto, both in Nagano prefecture so the one-way drop stays cheap. Rail and bus for everything else, because a car cannot help there: Kamikochi bans private vehicles, the Magome-Tsumago walk is point-to-point, and the long hauls at either end are faster by train.

legs.route: Hakuba to Azumino to Matsumoto, then return the car

todo.remarks: Do this first. Fewer than ten properties in the valley and the larch week sells out months ahead. Half board is the norm — there is nowhere else to eat after dark.
Second priority. Late October is the busiest stretch of the year on the Nakasendo and the houses have few rooms each. Book direct or through the Tsumago tourist office.
Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. Pick for the bath rather than the room — three nights and the plan barely leaves the property.
Three nights on one base, arriving as the long weekend empties out — all three are ordinary weekday nights, which is the point of travelling on the holiday rather than before it. Ask about laundry.
Near the castle or the station both work; Nakamachi is the nicer evening walk.

Two nights, near Nagano Station — the Togakushi bus and the car both leave from there and Zenkoji is 15 minutes up the road. Both nights are inside the Sports Day weekend, so book early; Zenkoji will be busier than a normal afternoon and the dawn service is the quiet alternative.

todo.task: Book Tokyo, 22 Oct — and check they hold luggage
todo.remarks: Shinagawa or Hamamatsucho, on the Haneda side. The whole last day depends on leaving the cases at the desk after checkout, so confirm it when booking rather than on the morning.
Landing at 22:15 — pick something inside or shuttle-linked to the terminal.
Waiting on an ANA promotion. Times in the file are the current timetable as at Aug 2026; the Oct 2027 schedule should load around Nov 2026, so confirm them before committing the rest.

todo.task: Reserve Hokuriku Shinkansen seats, Tokyo to Nagano, 9 Oct

todo.remarks: Every seat on the Nagano-Togakushi bus is reserved and online booking opens a month ahead, so around 10 Sep 2027. Eleven departures a day in green season, JPY 1,550 pp each way. IC cards like Suica are not accepted — cash or a contactless Visa on board. The Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass was discontinued in 2025.

todo.task: Book the hire car, Nagano 11 Oct to Matsumoto 14 Oct
todo.remarks: Four days, collected at Nagano Station and dropped at Matsumoto Station — same prefecture, so the one-way fee should be nil or near it; confirm that when booking rather than assuming. Azumino is visited on the drive down, so the car goes back at 16:00 on the 14th, before checking in at Matsumoto - no hotel parking needed there at all. Ask two more things at the desk: whether winter tyres are fitted by mid-October, since the Hakuba and Azumino roads run high, and whether an ETC card comes with it for the tolls.

todo.task: Reserve JR Shinano and Tokaido seats, Nagiso to Tokyo, 22 Oct
todo.remarks: Two legs, changing at Nagoya. Book them together so the oversized-baggage slot lands on the Tokaido half.

todo.task: Check the green-season Nagano to Hakuba bus timetable
todo.remarks: This sets day 2, not the shinkansen. Alpico run it from Bus Stop No. 26 at Nagano Station East Exit, 75-80 minutes, JPY 2,200-2,400 pp paid to the driver. Green season is about seven departures a day against sixteen in winter, so pick the bus first and work the morning backwards from it.

todo.task: Measure the cases against the Tokaido 160 cm rule
todo.remarks: Only matters for the Nagoya to Tokyo leg on 22 Oct. Height + width + depth of 160-250 cm needs a free oversized-baggage slot reserved with the seat; without one it is a JPY 1,000 charge at the gate. The Hokuriku Shinkansen on day 2 has no such rule.

todo.task: Check the last bus out of Kamikochi, 20 Oct
todo.remarks: The valley has no through road and the day ends early by late October.

todo.task: Arrange baggage forwarding, Matsumoto to Okuhida
todo.remarks: So Kamikochi only needs an overnight bag. Also book the Magome-Tsumago day-bag service for 21 Oct.

todo.task: Confirm the Tsugaike gondola is running, 13 Oct
todo.remarks: It took a maintenance closure in late October in a recent year. Worth a look before fixing the Hakuba days.

todo.task: Buy Tsugaike tickets at a Seven-Eleven
todo.remarks: JPY 3,300 per person instead of JPY 3,700 at the gate, including park entry.
Open-Meteo forecasts about 16 days. Until then the figures are Oct 2025 stand-ins, tagged as such. Kamikochi has no verified coordinates and will stay blank regardless.

todo.task: Grant the second traveller access to this trip
todo.remarks: Landing page, Who can edit panel, owner only. Until their email is ticked against this slug the whole private side is invisible to them.

todo.task: Confirm who is travelling and fix the names
todo.remarks: Seeded as CMC and a placeholder. Edit people on the Overview page.
Tsumago is at about 400 m and the Shinhotaka ropeway tops out at 2,156 m, where there will likely be snow. Layers rather than a second coat.
Happo Pond and the Nakasendo are walked rather than climbed, but check the policy does not exclude anything above 2,000 m.
